newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Volker Stevin upbeat on future prospects.
newsitem.headline: Volker Stevin upbeat on future prospects.

text.p: Dutch construction group Koninklijke Volker Stevin NV said on Wednesday it was upbeat on prospects in its main markets over the long term.
"In the next five to 10 years there looks to be no shortage of volume in building projects (on the Dutch market)," chairman Aad Baardewijk told a news conference.
Baardewijk said Volker Stevin, Dutch market leader in road-building, stood to benefit from the fact it derived some 85 percent of its turnover in the Netherlands.
He said the outlook for the Dutch housing market was favourable, while demand for offices and public buildings was also picking up. These activities account for some 40 percent of group turnover.
He said there was good demand for housing, which comprises a market of some 25 billion guilders in the Netherlands.

The bulk of Volker Stevin's housing turnover of some 450 million guilders annually was booked in the medium-range price segment (houses costing around 200,000 guilders) where the company realised "modest" profit margins of around 2-3 percent, Baardewijk said.
Demand in the civil engineering and road-building sector, which accounts for some 50 percent of Volker Stevin's turnover, was also favourable.
More infrastructural projects were coming onto the market although competition for them was fierce, he said.
The improved performance on the Dutch market helped offset lower turnover abroad, where the firm was hurt by sluggish markets in Belgium and the United Kingdom.
Turnover in the United States, where the company is mainly active in pipeline systems, was also down in the first half.

Finance director Pim Dijkman said demand was cyclical and sales had also been depressed by the fact that one of Volker Stevin's major clients, Washington National Gas, was in the midst of a merger with utility Puget Power.
"They have other things on their minds at the moment," he said.

The company earlier reported first-half profits from ordinary operations of 12.0 million guilders from a year-earlier 10.3 million. Net profit jumped to 16.1 million guilders, boosted by a 4.1 million guilder book profit on the sale of a stake in the Ecotech environmental services unit.
